title: Graphviz JSON Output: A Falsified Limitation Claim

story.text: This page records and falsifies an implicit limitation claim about Graphviz output capabilities in relation to Solo and Discourse Graphs.

Can Graphviz participate directly in a JSON-based data pipeline for Solo and Discourse Graphs, or is it limited to raster and vector image outputs?

(Optionally include links such as `[[Discourse Graphs]]`, `[[Graphviz Plugin]]`, or `[[Solo]]` to ensure neighbor reachability.)

Graphviz is not a bottleneck for Solo integration: it can emit native JSON representations of graphs, viz.js exposes this capability via a JavaScript API, and the FedWiki Graphviz plugin already transforms and publishes this data in a Solo-compatible form.

The Graphviz command-line interface can emit a native JSON representation of graphs (for example via a JSON output backend), not only raster or vector formats.

The viz.js WASM build exposes Graphviz’s JSON output through a JavaScript API, making the internal graph structure accessible in the browser.

Recent versions of the FedWiki Graphviz plugin include an internal transformation from Graphviz’s native JSON representation to the JSON structure expected by the Solo plugin.

This transformed data is exposed via functions and CSS classes in the DOM, allowing Solo to retrieve it using the same conventional source-discovery mechanism used for other FedWiki plugins.

Graphviz is effectively limited to raster or vector image outputs; therefore, Graphviz diagrams cannot directly participate in a JSON-based data pipeline for Solo without post-hoc parsing of SVG or DOT.
Status: falsified by existing Graphviz JSON backends, viz.js API exposure, and the current implementation of the FedWiki Graphviz plugin.

item.title: Graphviz JSON Output: A Falsified Limitation Claim

item.text:
Below is a **tightened, audit-grade “claim + falsification” formulation** suitable for direct insertion into Zettel 7977. It is written to be addressable, falsifiable, and repo-anchored.

---

## Claim–Falsification Record (Zettel 7977)

### Earlier Claim C4 (implicit, now falsified)

**C4**
Graphviz is effectively limited to raster or vector image outputs; therefore, Graphviz diagrams cannot directly participate in a JSON-based data pipeline for Solo without post-hoc parsing of SVG or DOT.

**Status**
❌ Falsified

---

### Falsifying Evidence E4

**E4.1 — Graphviz JSON backend**
The Graphviz command-line interface can emit a *native JSON representation* of graphs (e.g. via `-Tjson`), not only raster (`png`, `jpg`) or vector (`svg`, `pdf`) formats.

**E4.2 — viz.js WASM API**
The viz.js WASM build exposes this JSON-emitting capability through its JavaScript API, making Graphviz’s internal graph structure programmatically accessible in the browser.

**E4.3 — Existing transformation in wiki-plugin-graphviz**
Recent versions of the Graphviz plugin already include an internal transformation that converts Graphviz’s *native JSON* into the *Solo-compatible JSON representation*.

*Repository anchor:*
`wiki-plugin-graphviz/client/graphviz.js`, lines 17–107
[https://github.com/fedwiki/wiki-plugin-graphviz/blob/1366fad/client/graphviz.js#L17-L107](https://github.com/fedwiki/wiki-plugin-graphviz/blob/1366fad/client/graphviz.js#L17-L107)

**E4.4 — DOM exposure for Solo consumption**
The transformed JSON data is exposed via functions and CSS classes in the DOM, where the Solo plugin can retrieve it using the same conventional “source API” pattern employed by other FedWiki plugins.

*Repository anchor:*
`wiki-plugin-graphviz/client/graphviz.js`, lines 582–584
[https://github.com/fedwiki/wiki-plugin-graphviz/blob/1366fad/client/graphviz.js#L582-L584](https://github.com/fedwiki/wiki-plugin-graphviz/blob/1366fad/client/graphviz.js#L582-L584)

---

### Revised Claim C4′ (post-correction)

**C4′**
Graphviz is *not* a bottleneck for Solo integration: it can emit structured JSON, viz.js exposes this in JavaScript, and the FedWiki Graphviz plugin already translates and publishes this data in a Solo-consumable form. Any remaining limitations are therefore architectural or UX-level (wiring, discovery, freeze/thaw semantics), not representational.

---

### Implication for the Zettel cluster

This falsification shifts the problem statement:

* from **“Graphviz cannot provide the right data”**
* to **“we are not yet exploiting the data Graphviz already provides.”**

That implication aligns directly with Eric’s correction and reframes the “model Graphviz behavior off Map plugin UX” discussion as a **reuse and exposure problem**, not a capability gap.
